contract_plain_english: For independent mean-zero sub-exponential variables, normalize their sum by 1/sqrt N. The display gives a quadratic upper-tail bound below C sqrt N and a literal coefficient-one linear bound 2 exp(-t sqrt N) above C sqrt N, while footnote 9 permits c and C to depend on K. The preceding theorem instead supplies a K-dependent coefficient in the large exponent, and the source does not resolve that discrepancy.
